cards.explanation: She's about to give birth. The very next verse says she was pregnant and crying out in the pain and agony of giving birth. She's dressed in the sun and the moon is at her feet, but the real action is still what's happening with her child. Friends, a glow-up never changes the fact that there's work to do, and I've seen that in my bakery.

The second sign is a huge red dragon, with seven heads, ten horns and seven royal crowns on his heads. The woman is called a sign, and so is he, and that's a lot of sign for one sky. Both signs appear in heaven. Bakers, you can tell this guy is trouble without any help from me.

The answer is False. It's not every last star. Verse 4 says his tail swept a third of the stars from the sky, hurling them to the earth. One swish of a tail and a third of the stars are gone, friends. Even so, the text keeps the number exactly where it is, so we do too.

The dragon stands there to devour her child as soon as it's born. The text says he stood before the woman who was about to give birth, ready to devour her child as soon as she gave birth. He wasn't there for the view, friends. I think the whole scene gets very quiet right here, and it's a hard one to sit with.

The answer is False. The dragon is ready and waiting, but verse 5 says her child was caught up to God and to His throne. That's where the text takes the child. I'd love to have seen the look on all seven faces, friends.

The answer is wilderness. The woman fled there, to a place God had prepared for her. The place was ready before she got there, bakers. That's the kind of detail I appreciate, because I like it when the oven is already warm.

The answer is True. Verse 8 says the dragon was not strong enough, and no longer was any place found in heaven for him and his angels. Michael and his angels fought, the dragon and his angels fought back, and the dragon still came up short. Friends, a guy with seven heads and he still can't win.

The dragon is that ancient serpent called the devil. Verse 9 says the great dragon is that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. John, who wrote this book, doesn't leave us guessing, friends. The dragon is named plainly, and that settles it.

The reason is that the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down. The voice says, “For the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down…” and goes on to say he accuses them day and night before our God. His being hurled out of heaven is why the voice announces it now. When the accuser is out, friends, the announcement can come.

They conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony. The voice says, “They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony.” The Lamb is Jesus, whom John the Baptist called the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin (John 1:29). The voice names His blood and the word of their testimony, friends.

The word is rejoice. The voice says, “Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them!” The accuser has been thrown down, so the heavens get to celebrate. Friends, I'd be tossing sprinkles right now if my planet had a heaven nearby.

The answer is True. The voice says, “But woe to the earth and the sea; with great fury the devil has come down to you, knowing he has only a short time.” He's been thrown down, and now he's here. It's a serious line, friends, so I'd read it slowly.

The answer is True. Verse 13 says that when the dragon saw he had been thrown to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child. He lost the war in heaven and went right after her. Some folks lose and walk it off, bakers. He doesn't.

She's given two wings of a great eagle. Verse 14 says she was given them to fly from the presence of the serpent to her place in the wilderness. Notice, friends, the verse says she was given the wings.

The earth opens up and swallows the river. Verse 16 says the earth helped the woman and opened its mouth to swallow up the river that the dragon had poured from his mouth. The ground itself steps in on her side, friends. I love it when the floor shows up to help.

The answer is False. Verse 17 says the dragon was enraged at the woman and went to make war with the rest of her children, who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus. The text has him going to make war with them, not going back to fight Michael. His anger takes him toward them, friends.
